content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

model_essay.title: The Lasting Impact of Teachers
model_essay.content:
It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development. Indeed, a dedicated teacher does far more than deliver knowledge — he or she shapes the way students think, communicate, and perceive the world.

From an academic perspective, teachers ignite curiosity and cultivate critical thinking. My high-school chemistry teacher, for instance, encouraged us to design our own experiments rather than merely memorize formulas. That approach not only deepened our understanding of the subject but also fostered a lifelong love of inquiry.

Beyond academics, teachers serve as role models who mold character. Through patience, fairness, and encouragement, they teach students resilience, empathy, and integrity — qualities that prove invaluable in later life.

In conclusion, the influence of teachers extends well beyond the classroom. By nurturing both intellect and character, they leave an indelible mark on every student they encounter, and society as a whole benefits from their dedication.

structure_analysis.opening: 以题目给定句开篇，随即提出核心论点：优秀教师的影响远超知识传授，涵盖思维方式与世界观的塑造。
structure_analysis.body: 分两个层面展开论述：第一层从学术角度出发，以高中化学老师鼓励自主实验为例，说明教师能激发好奇心与批判性思维；第二层从品格培养角度出发，阐述教师通过耐心、公正和鼓励塑造学生的韧性、共情力和正直品质。
structure_analysis.closing: 总结全文，强调教师的影响力超越课堂，兼顾智识与品格的培养，最终惠及整个社会。

highlights: 论点明确，开篇紧扣题目要求，自然引出中心思想
采用学术与品格双线并行的结构，层次清晰，论证充分
运用个人经历（化学老师的例子）增强说服力和真实感
结尾升华主题，将教师影响从个人层面提升至社会层面

transcript.text: One thing I've learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample grey areas in human behaviour, and that there may not always be clear right or wrong solutions to employee disputes.
transcript.translation: 在管理岗位上工作二十五年，我学到的一点是，人类行为中存在许多灰色地带，员工纠纷的解决方案并非总是清晰的是非对错。

transcript.text: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
transcript.translation: 当两个人对同一事件有不同版本时，很难知道该相信谁。

transcript.text: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
transcript.translation: 有一件事总是让我想起。

transcript.text: It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
transcript.translation: 那是多年前的事了，这场冲突如此不值得记忆，以至于我甚至记不清纠纷的具体内容，但我绝对记得解决方案。

transcript.text: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth.
transcript.translation: 两位有才华的年轻高管，其中一位由我管理，对同一事件有截然不同的说法，看来我们永远无法得知真相。

transcript.text: We reached a deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.
transcript.translation: 我们陷入了僵局，另一位高管的经理说：“这是我从一位我曾经共事的优秀经理那里学到的。”

transcript.text: He used to say, And just like that, we had a path forward.
transcript.translation: 他过去常说，就这样，我们找到了前进的道路。

transcript.text: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
transcript.translation: 我和我的同事一致认为，我们可能永远无法查明事情的真相。

transcript.text: Quite likely, there were elements of truth in both employees' stories.
transcript.translation: 很可能，两位员工的故事中都有真实的成分。

transcript.text: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
transcript.translation: 我们同意今后监控他们的行动和关系，但不再进一步干预。

transcript.text: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
transcript.translation: 我们对双方都做了最善意的假设，然后继续前进。

transcript.text: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
transcript.translation: 结果是，我们能够将冲突抛在脑后。

transcript.text: In fact, their problems didn't recur.
transcript.translation: 事实上，他们的问题没有再次发生。

transcript.text: Over the years, this general approach has proved useful.
transcript.translation: 多年来，这种通用方法被证明是有效的。

transcript.text: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
transcript.translation: 每当真相不明时，假设积极意图并同意继续前进可能是一个建设性的决定。

transcript.text: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for.

transcript.text: For others, it's just a daily occurrence.
transcript.translation: 对另一些人来说，这只是一个日常事件。

transcript.text: And that second group of people is becoming the majority, as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
transcript.translation: 而第二组人正在成为多数，因为喜欢烹饪的美国人数量在减少。

transcript.text: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking.
transcript.translation: 在21世纪初，研究员Eddie Yoon进行了一项调查，以确定美国人对烹饪的态度。

transcript.text: The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook, and 35% reported mixed feelings.
transcript.translation: 调查发现，15%的美国人热爱烹饪，50%的人表示讨厌烹饪，35%的人报告有复杂感受。

transcript.text: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it, and 45% had mixed feelings.
transcript.translation: 当Yoon在15年后进行相同调查时，只有10%的受访者表示热爱烹饪，45%的人表示讨厌它，45%的人有复杂感受。

transcript.text: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
transcript.translation: Yoon断言烹饪类似于缝纫。

transcript.text: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
transcript.translation: 就在20世纪初，许多美国人自己缝制衣服。

transcript.text: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing.
transcript.translation: 如今，绝大多数美国人购买衣服。

transcript.text: Only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby.
transcript.translation: 只有极少数人仍然缝纫，而且他们主要是作为爱好来做。

transcript.text: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
transcript.translation: Yoon相信家庭厨师的数量将以类似方式减少。

transcript.text: Currently, the average American household spends over $3 ,000 per year on dining out.
transcript.translation: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上花费超过3000美元。

transcript.text: However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash.
transcript.translation: 然而，人们在便利上节省的，在现金上却损失了。

transcript.text: Take buying lunch on work days, for example.
transcript.translation: 以工作日买午餐为例。

transcript.text: People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
transcript.translation: 当人们买午餐时，平均每餐花费10美元。

transcript.text: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
transcript.translation: 与此同时，自己做午餐会花费更少。

transcript.text: One survey found people only spend, on average, $6.
transcript.translation: 一项调查发现，人们平均每餐只花费6美元。

transcript.text: 30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
transcript.translation: 当他们带家里准备的午餐时，只花费30。

transcript.text: Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
transcript.translation: 美国人对在厨房花时间的日益厌恶标志着杂货行业面临的一系列挑战。

transcript.text: It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.

transcript.text: 5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing.
transcript.translation: 5亿个行李箱被托运行李，其中2600万个丢失。

transcript.text: And of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
transcript.translation: 在这2600万个中，有100万个从未归还原主。

transcript.text: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
transcript.translation: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，以及一些人 simply 忘记取走自己的行李箱，是其中几个原因。

transcript.text: But the number one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
transcript.translation: 但行李箱丢失的首要原因是它没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。

transcript.text: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates, to arrival gates, to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
transcript.translation: 将行李箱从值机处转运到登机口、到达口、再到行李认领处，是一项时机精妙的工作。

transcript.text: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights.
transcript.translation: 如果系统移动太慢，行李箱就赶不上转机航班。

transcript.text: If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
transcript.translation: 如果它太快，行李箱可能赶上转机，但乘客可能会错过航班。

transcript.text: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
transcript.translation: 每个机场都有自己分配行李箱在转运中所需时间的方式。

transcript.text: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
transcript.translation: 一些机场拥有先进的自动化系统，包括读取行李标签的扫描仪、无需停靠即可装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及将行李路由到适当登机口的分拣机。

transcript.text: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
transcript.translation: 即便如此，所有这些技术可能无法防止你的行李标签在传送带上被撕掉，使你成为没有名字的行李箱的主人。

transcript.text: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared mishandled by the carrier.
transcript.translation: 一旦行李箱丢失，乘客提出索赔，该行李箱就被承运商宣布为处理不当。

transcript.text: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged.
transcript.translation: 处理不当指的是被延误、丢失、偷窃或损坏的行李箱。

transcript.text: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
transcript.translation: 大多数延误的行李箱只比主人晚一个航班，可以在24小时内送达。

transcript.text: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination.
transcript.translation: 其他行李箱由航空公司员工检查，以寻找其所有权和目的地的线索。

transcript.text: If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
transcript.translation: 如果谜团解开，那些行李箱会在四五天内归还给主人。

transcript.text: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
transcript.translation: 没有目的地代码或身份标签的行李箱被运送到中央仓库，并在接下来的90天内经历全面的行李追踪过程。

transcript.text: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions.
transcript.translation: 航空公司清点其处理不当的行李箱，许多使用数据库将内容与主人的描述匹配。

transcript.text: It takes about three months to go from missing in action to irretrievably lost.
transcript.translation: 从丢失到无法找回的丢失大约需要三个月。

transcript.text: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
transcript.translation: 一旦发生这种情况，行李箱会被捐赠给慈善机构、拍卖，或由公司购买后向公众出售。

transcript.text: So, never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage, and make sure your name is on the bag along with your phone number so an agent can contact you.
transcript.translation: 所以，永远不要在托运行李中打包任何真正有价值的东西，并确保你的名字和电话号码在行李箱上，以便代理人能联系你。

transcript.text: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone, and you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
transcript.translation: 你可能曾遇到过有人在与你互动时只顾玩手机而忽略你，而且你自己也可能做过类似的事。

transcript.text: In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
transcript.translation: 在最近的一项调查中，十分之九的受访者表示，他们在最近一次社交活动中使用了智能手机。

transcript.text: There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
transcript.translation: 还有证据表明，这种行为对社会有害。

transcript.text: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
transcript.translation: 这会让人们对面对面的交流感到不那么满意，并可能产生怨恨和嫉妒的情绪。

transcript.text: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
transcript.translation: 现在，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨这些影响的原因。

transcript.text: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
transcript.translation: 该研究包括128名以女性为主的学生参与者。

transcript.text: The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
transcript.translation: 参与者观看了一个三分钟的动画，其中两个卡通人物互动并进行了对话。

transcript.text: The conversation couldn't be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
transcript.translation: 对话无法听到，但可以通过嘴部动作来识别。

transcript.text: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
transcript.translation: 参与者必须想象自己是视频中最接近的人物，然后对对话以及他们对对话伙伴的感受做出判断。

transcript.text: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participant's conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
transcript.translation: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的对话伙伴的手机在对话过程中一直放在桌上未使用。

transcript.text: In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
transcript.translation: 在另一个版本中，他们的伙伴的注意力很快被手机上的某物吸引，并在剩余时间里与手机互动。

transcript.text: A third version involved the participant's partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
transcript.translation: 第三个版本涉及参与者的伙伴在手机互动和忽视手机的时段之间交替。

transcript.text: If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
transcript.translation: 如果你经历过类似的情况，你可能不会对实验结果感到惊讶。

transcript.text: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
transcript.translation: 参与者对社交互动中的手机使用持负面看法。

transcript.text: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
transcript.translation: 手机出现得越多，他们认为互动质量和关系质量就越差。

transcript.text: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion.
transcript.translation: 研究人员认为，专注于手机而不是身边的人会产生这种效果，因为这被视为一种社会排斥形式。

transcript.text: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
transcript.translation: 他们断言，这种行为类似于人们别无选择只能在学校的自助餐厅独自用餐。

transcript.text: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
transcript.translation: 转折在于，这种排斥发生在共享物理接触和进行对话的同时。

transcript.text: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning, and self-esteem.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊心产生了不利影响。

transcript.text: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
transcript.translation: 这些负面影响类似于传统社会排斥形式所引起的。

transcript.text: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.
transcript.translation: 新发现很重要，因为它们详细阐述了我们对日常经验中微妙但常见方面的理解。

transcript.text: This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
transcript.translation: 这种常见行为即使在我们试图与他人建立联系时，也可能造成疏离的恶性循环。

transcript.text: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons.
transcript.translation: 越来越多的人出于各种原因旅行。

transcript.text: Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business.
transcript.translation: 许多是游客，但也有很多人出于个人或公务出差。

transcript.text: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
transcript.translation: 无论旅行的原因是什么，旅行者们的一个常见抱怨是他们找到的住宿缺乏人情味。

transcript.text: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited.
transcript.translation: 在五个相似的酒店连续住五晚后，商务旅行者可能很难记住每天发生了什么，甚至记不清去了哪些城镇。

transcript.text: And the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
transcript.translation: 而游客可能会错误地认为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装饰、食物和服务方面是如此。

transcript.text: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or bed and breakfast arrangements.
transcript.translation: 为了对抗这种缺乏个性的相似感，旅行者们开始利用家庭式款待或住宿加早餐的安排。

transcript.text: B&Bs, I mean bed and breakfast arrangements, are private homes, which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalised, friendly setting.
transcript.translation: 住宿加早餐安排是私人住宅，在非常个性化、友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐。

transcript.text: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic ways of visit Europe, especially the British Isles, and in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
transcript.translation: 几十年来，住宿加早餐一直是游览欧洲，尤其是不列颠群岛的经典方式，事实上，它们在美国并不是一个新概念。

transcript.text: The tradition dates back to colonial times, when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
transcript.translation: 这一传统可以追溯到殖民时代，那时旅馆稀少，疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的善意来获得一顿饭和一张床。

transcript.text: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
transcript.translation: 但住宿加早餐作为理想住宿的复兴是相当近期的现象。

transcript.text: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
transcript.translation: 如果经营住宿加早餐的想法引起了你的兴趣，那么在投身这一业务之前，有几个因素需要考虑。

transcript.text: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.
transcript.translation: 第一个考虑因素是你的房产，不仅是建筑本身，还有位置。

transcript.text: If you live near a famous historical site, or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington DC, your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B.
transcript.translation: 如果你住在著名的历史遗址附近，或热门目的地，如纽约市或华盛顿特区，你的家可以相当简单，但作为住宿加早餐仍然能经营得很好。

transcript.text: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique, or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath, or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
transcript.translation: 另一方面，如果你的家在建筑上独特，或有旅行者设施，如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意长途跋涉来你这里。

transcript.text: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
transcript.translation: 另一个重要因素是你和你家人的生活方式。

transcript.text: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry, and bookkeeping involved.
transcript.translation: 你必须考虑家庭成员是否真正喜欢访客，是否愿意反复讨论当地景点和活动，以及是否有时间和精力处理额外的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和簿记工作。

transcript.text: The final consideration is a financial one.
transcript.translation: 最后一个考虑因素是财务方面。

transcript.text: Potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
transcript.translation: 潜在的住宿加早餐房东必须对收入机会持现实态度。

transcript.text: While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
transcript.translation: 虽然住宿加早餐通常初始成本较低，但专家估计，房东至少需要定期出租五个房间才能从中谋生。

paragraphs.text: It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a __26__ for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.
paragraphs.translation: 最好将口音理解为一种独特、系统且有规则可循的说话方式。口音并非方言的同义词，但两者有所关联。方言是一个总括性术语，涵盖一个社区的发音、造词和词语排序方式；而口音仅涉及发音部分。

paragraphs.text: Many __27__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is __28__ the best form of speech, but linguists often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __29__. In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.
paragraphs.translation: 许多外行认为每个国家都有一种单一的标准说话方式，以及一种单一的标准口音，并且这种感知到的标准本质上是最佳的言语形式，但语言学家常常指出，标准口音的概念最好理解为一种理想而非现实。换句话说，没有人说“标准英语”；相反，它是一种想象的语言使用方式，只存在于语法和风格书籍中。

paragraphs.text: One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been __30__ supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the __31__ have never consistently held to those standards anyway.
paragraphs.translation: 语言学家认为没有唯一真正标准的一个原因是，多年来，有多种所谓的标准，取决于时间和地点。例如，1950年代英国新闻片中英语的标准与今天美国国家新闻广播中的标准大不相同。事实上，从未有一个单一的标准被完全认同——而且各种广播机构也从未始终如一地遵循那些标准。

paragraphs.text: Even so, this idea of a standard accent is __32__ and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that __33__ from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern U.S. accent features are more accepted in __34__ such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may __35__ with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.
paragraphs.translation: 即便如此，标准口音的观念仍然具有影响力，许多工作场所和教育环境延续了这样的想法：偏离当前标准的口音不太合适，甚至不合适。学者们发现，美国南部口音特征在政府、法律和面向服务的工作场所等领域更易被接受，但在技术领域接受度较低。非标准口音的可接受性可能与阶级和文化的差异相关，较新或声望较高的行业期望工作场所使用更标准的言语。

questionGroups.title: The History and Meaning of Colored Traffic Lights

material.title: The History and Meaning of Colored Traffic Lights

paragraphs.text: Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion and 20% off air pollution. Congestion costs time, money, and lives. Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!
paragraphs.translation: 定时交通信号灯根据计划设置，旨在与高峰交通时段协调。城市需要至少每两年监控和更新信号灯时间表，以保持这些系统有效。在加利福尼亚州洛杉矶，一个雄心勃勃的项目进一步同步洛杉矶的每一个红绿灯，耗资超过4亿美元。问问该市的居民，他们可能会同意在路上节省时间是值得的。如果在全国实施，同步可以减少10%的交通拥堵和20%的空气污染。拥堵消耗时间、金钱和生命。大数据可以帮助改善数百万人安全共享道路的方式。然而，没有交通信号灯，这一切都不可能实现！

paragraphs.text: The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective. It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.
paragraphs.translation: 第一个交通信号灯于19世纪60年代在伦敦发明，但几乎无法辨认或有效。它是由铁路经理约翰·皮克·奈特在1868年从铁路信号系统改编而来。铁路在夜间使用红色燃气灯示意停止，白天使用绿色燃气灯。奈特在1868年12月于伦敦威斯敏斯特桥附近安装了一个类似的燃气灯信号系统。

paragraphs.text: The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.
paragraphs.translation: 第一个交通信号灯的使用寿命很短。安装后一个月内，燃气泄漏导致一个信号灯在其警察操作员身上爆炸。

paragraphs.text: Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident. Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States. London would not see another traffic light until 1929.
paragraphs.translation: 在伦敦事件后，交通信号灯的自动化停滞了。四十年后，汽车涌入城市街道才促使美国发展交通信号灯。伦敦直到1929年才再次出现交通信号灯。

paragraphs.text: The United States is a car culture like no other country. Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.
paragraphs.translation: 美国是一个独特的汽车文化国家。与大多数欧洲城市在马匹是高科技时开始城市规划不同，美国许多城市是围绕城市扩张、郊区开发和汽车设计的。

paragraphs.text: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. The first traffic signals were semaphores. Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. They could be manual or automatic. There was no consistent design. Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.
paragraphs.translation: 随着交通和城市的发展，解决日益增长的交通问题的竞赛也在加剧。最初的交通信号是信号灯。信号灯是带有移动臂的塔，示意交通停止或通行。它们可以是手动或自动的。没有统一的设计。随着需求的出现，各种型号被发明并安装在城市中。

paragraphs.text: In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South. He developed a manually switched stop light. The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer. The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights.
paragraphs.translation: 1912年，莱斯特·怀尔是一名警察，因Main Street和200 South的交通而疲惫不堪。他开发了一个手动切换的停车灯。这个四面盒子，安装在一根十英尺高的杆子上，看起来像一个鸟舍，由一名警官手动操作。警官会翻动开关，在倾斜的红灯和绿灯之间切换。

paragraphs.text: Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words. However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell. The words "stop" or "move" were on lights. The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection. It was not automated, though. A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches.
paragraphs.translation: 与1910年的信号灯一样，第一个电信号使用文字。然而，文字不再写在升降的臂上。文字“停止”或“移动”在灯上。柱子照亮了交叉路口周围的四个角柱。不过，它不是自动的。需要一个带操作员的亭子来翻动开关。

paragraphs.text: The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner. From that vantage, an officer could oversee the crowd. If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights. The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly. Finally, in San Francisco, the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.
paragraphs.translation: 该系统允许警察从街道中间移动到角落。从那个制高点，警官可以监督人群。如果有紧急车辆来，警官可以翻动开关，通过触发所有红灯来清空交叉路口。紧急车辆现在可以轻松通过。最终，在旧金山，第一个可以自动（或手动）操作的红绿灯系统于1917年推出。

paragraphs.text: In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit — also known as Motor City, USA. The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City. Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed). Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.
paragraphs.translation: 1920年，第一个三色灯系统在底特律推出——底特律也被称为美国汽车城。交通信号灯的发展没有比汽车城更合适的背景了。福特汽车公司于1903年在底特律成立（其他汽车公司随后跟进）。福特通过创建大规模工厂生产，使汽车对普通人而非富人来说更可负担。

paragraphs.text: Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections. Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse-drawn carriages, and street cars. The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.
paragraphs.translation: 对于飞驰过交叉路口的新数量汽车来说，停止和通行信号不够。街道上充满了新的汽车数量，还有送货马车、拥挤的人群、自行车、马拉车和电车。引入警示性黄灯有助于提高驾驶员安全性，减少闯红灯造成的事故。

paragraphs.text: Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets. Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951. The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899.
paragraphs.translation: 在混乱的城市街道上，停车灯极其重要。人行横道直到1951年才引入。美国第一次行人死亡事故发生在1899年。

paragraphs.text: The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States. In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal. The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system. The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.
paragraphs.translation: 现代交通信号灯的发展可能始于伦敦，但它在美国成长。在克利夫兰，一位名叫加勒特·摩根的非裔美国发明家提出了一个负担得起的、有专利的交通信号。黄灯使交叉路口比旧的停止和通行系统更安全。新设计足够便宜，允许安装更多的灯。

paragraphs.text: Morgan sold the patent to General Electric — and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted. Green means go. It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. It does not mean full-throttle ahead. While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents. Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop. Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right. You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way. In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated. New York City does not allow a right on red.
paragraphs.translation: 摩根将专利卖给了通用电气——交通信号灯的传播因此被放行。绿色意味着通行。就这么简单，但最好还是检查两边是否有不注意或闯红灯的来车。黄色意味着减速并准备停止。它不代表全速前进。虽然你可能侥幸冲过交叉路口，但闯黄灯可能导致罚单和危险事故。红灯是明确且一致的停止警告。即使在允许红灯右转的地方，你也必须在右转前完全停止。你还必须让行任何有优先通行权的直行交通。在大多数州和城市，除非另有指示，否则你可以红灯右转。纽约市不允许红灯右转。

paragraphs.text: Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states. The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn. However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming.
paragraphs.translation: 红箭头意味着在大多数州你不能红灯右转。在这些情况下，绿箭头是你唯一可以转弯的时候。然而，在伊利诺伊州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、马里兰州、密歇根州、新罕布什尔州、北达科他州、俄勒冈州、南卡罗来纳州、犹他州、华盛顿州和怀俄明州，你可以在完全停止后红灯右转。

paragraphs.text: Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic. When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop. Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn. Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station. There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States. If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic.
paragraphs.translation: 闪烁红灯与停车标志相同，通常用于交通最小的四向交叉路口。当到达闪烁红灯时，进行完全停止。闪烁红箭头类似地意味着停止然后继续转弯。闪烁黄灯意味着让行或警示，如在消防站外。没有全方向闪烁黄灯，因为在美国被禁止。如果你有闪烁黄灯，你必须让行来车。

paragraphs.text: Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light. These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow. When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop. In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending. The red arrow is about to start. Vehicles should stop if safely possible. Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow.
paragraphs.translation: 闪烁黄箭头是四信号交通灯的一部分。在一些州，这些用于受保护绿色转弯信号或箭头之后，但在稳定黄箭头之前。当显示闪烁黄箭头时，你可以在让行行人和交通后转弯。稳定黄箭头在三灯信号中保持正常的黄灯警示，意味着停止或准备停止。在具有闪烁黄箭头的四信号系统中，稳定黄箭头是让行期即将结束的信号。红箭头即将开始。如果安全可能，车辆应停止。闯稳定黄箭头可能导致交通罚单。

paragraphs.text: Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution). Yellow means caution and yield. Red means danger and stop. Always drive defensively and obey traffic signal.
paragraphs.translation: 交通信号灯的含义总体上相当一致，但有各种偏差。绿色意味着可以安全通行（尽管仍应谨慎）。黄色意味着小心和让行。红色意味着危险和停止。始终防御性驾驶并遵守交通信号。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: Upon seeing a flashing yellow arrow, a driver should let pedestrians and traffic pass first before taking the turn.
questions.analysis: 题目说看到闪烁黄色箭头时需先让行人和车辆通过再转弯。Q段提到"When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic"，与题意完全吻合。

questions.statementText: The red and green automatic traffic light system originated in an American city.
questions.analysis: 题目说红绿自动交通信号灯系统起源于一座美国城市。I段末尾提到"in San Francisco, the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917"，对应该信息。

questions.statementText: Residents of an American city tend to share the opinion that time saved on the road justifies the cost of upgrading its traffic light system.
questions.analysis: 题目说某美国城市的居民认为节省在路上的时间值得花费升级交通灯系统的成本。A段提到洛杉矶花费超过4亿美元同步红绿灯，并说"Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it"。

questions.statementText: Mass production of cars made it possible for ordinary people to buy them.
questions.analysis: 题目说汽车的大规模生产使普通人也能购买。J段提到"Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production"，与题意一致。

questions.statementText: What a traffic light means is almost the same everywhere despite some variations.
questions.analysis: 题目说交通灯的含义几乎各地相同，尽管有一些变化。R段开头指出"Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations"，直接对应。

questions.statementText: Pedestrian crossings came into being only in the mid-twentieth century.
questions.analysis: 题目说人行横道直到20世纪中期才出现。L段提到"Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951"，1951年正是20世纪中叶，与题意吻合。

questions.statementText: People raced to address increasing traffic problems along with the expansion of cities and traffic.
questions.analysis: 题目说随着城市和交通的扩张，人们竞相解决日益增长的交通问题。F段开头说"As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems"，完全对应。

questions.statementText: When the warning yellow light was introduced, driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced.
questions.analysis: 题目说引入警示黄灯后驾驶变得更安全，交通事故减少。K段提到"The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights"，直接对应。

questions.statementText: The signal system on the railroad served as the basis for the first traffic light.
questions.analysis: 题目说铁路信号系统是第一个交通灯的基础。B段提到"It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager"，说明交通灯是从铁路信号系统改造而来。

questions.statementText: Even though a green light signals "go", attention should be paid to traffic on either side in case some driver is being careless or ignoring a red light.
questions.analysis: 题目说即使绿灯亮了也应注意两侧来车以防有人闯红灯。N段提到"Green means go...but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light"，与题意吻合。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
paragraphs.translation: 正念已被证明具有许多显著的健康益处——它可以帮助减轻焦虑，并促进慢性病患者的康复。

paragraphs.text: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
paragraphs.translation: 这种实践基于古印度佛教经典中首次描述的一种见解，即人类有能力观察经验而不陷入其中。这简单地意味着，我们可以观察到自己有渴望、快乐的想法，甚至恐惧的情绪，而不会在当下做出反应，以免放大这种感觉或让思绪陷入回忆过去或预想未来。

paragraphs.text: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
paragraphs.translation: 这种正念实践可以帮助我们平静心灵和身体，因为我们学会了不对经验做出喜好或好坏的判断反应。它不会使我们变得冷漠或无动于衷，而是让我们更加全然地临在。

paragraphs.text: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
paragraphs.translation: 在我们当代世界中实践正念的挑战之一是人类注意力发生了深刻转变。艺术家珍妮·奥德尔认为，在我们的“注意力经济”中，人类的注意力已经被转化为一种商品，供大公司买卖。这种经济建立在手机和社交媒体的技术革命之上，使得公司能够在每个时刻用他们的内容瞄准我们的注意力。

paragraphs.text: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
paragraphs.translation: 大多数人使用的设备是对当下时刻的永久干扰。结果是，我们可能会感觉专注和全然临在的能力被偷走了。但正念可以帮助我们抵制注意力经济，并享受那些让生活特别的事物，比如与我们所爱的人在一起。

paragraphs.text: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
paragraphs.translation: 大多数正念研究关注实践对个人的益处，但一些学者主张，我们不仅可以为自己实践正念，还可以为他人实践。它可以帮助我们建立更强大、更健康的关系。

paragraphs.text: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
paragraphs.translation: 可悲的事实是，生活在注意力经济中，我们大多数人都成了糟糕的倾听者。然而，正如我们可以观察自己拥有一个经验而不做出反应一样，我们也可以观察另一个人拥有一个经验，而不陷入反应性和判断。

paragraphs.text: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
paragraphs.translation: 正念的礼物是一种带着同情心倾听他人描述他们经验的实践。给予这份礼物意味着收起手机、关闭社交媒体，并放下其他常见的干扰。它意味着练习在他人面前全然临在，以完全的注意力倾听他们，而不做判断，同时抵制让互动围绕自己的冲动。

paragraphs.text: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.
paragraphs.translation: 如果我们根据价格来判断礼物的价值，这份礼物可能看起来毫无价值，但在一个分心的世界里，它是一份珍贵的礼物。

options.text: People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold.

options.label: C
options.text: Businesses profit from selling mobile phones and revolutionizing social media.

options.text: People tend to purchase products and services without careful thinking.

questions.keySentence: The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.

wrongOptions.A: 原文讨论的是注意力被商品化，而非技术进步更新产品和服务。
wrongOptions.C: 原文说手机和社媒是技术手段使企业能瞄准人们的注意力，并非企业靠卖手机获利。

questions.questionText: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media?

options.label: B
options.text: They render users incapable of resisting temptation.

options.label: C
options.text: They rob users of their ability to observe experience.

options.label: D
options.text: They tempt users to endorse the attention economy.

wrongOptions.B: 原文说设备持续分散注意力，并非说用户无法抵抗诱惑。

questions.questionText: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: It shifts our attention from material things to spiritual pursuits.

options.label: C
options.text: It is conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships.

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 第六段指出一些学者认为我们不仅可以为自己练习正念，还可以为他人练习，这有助于建立更强健的人际关系。C选项"有助于建立更好的人际关系"直接对应原文。A选项说防止对他人做武断判断，虽有关联但不是原文强调的主要益处；B选项说将注意力从物质转向精神追求，原文未提及；D选项说重获享受生活的能力，也并非此处论述重点。
questions.keySentence: It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.

wrongOptions.A: 虽然正念涉及不做评判，但本题问的是学者提到的益处，原文明确说的是建立更好的关系。
wrongOptions.B: 原文未提及将注意力从物质转向精神追求。

options.label: A
options.text: Share each other's experience frankly and compassionately.

options.label: B

options.label: C

wrongOptions.B: 原文说全神贯注地倾听，而非全神贯注地建立亲密关系。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
paragraphs.translation: 前几天，我不得不登录一个以前从未使用过的服务。由于我是新用户，网站决定需要确认我不是机器人，因此给我设置了一个验证码测试，以确定用户是人还是机器。

paragraphs.text: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
paragraphs.translation: 我看到一张路边场景的图像，上面覆盖着一个网格。我的“挑战”是点击网格中包含交通标志的每个单元格。我这样做了，有点恼火。然后，我又看到另一张图像和另一个网格——同样要求识别路标。我像羔羊一样顺从了，之后网站接受了我的输入。

paragraphs.text: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labour to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
paragraphs.translation: 然后我意识到，我一直在做的事情是为训练引导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件添加数据集。因此，为了获得一个将从我的输入中获利的自动化服务，我首先必须做一些无偿劳动，以帮助提高自动驾驶车辆的性能。

paragraphs.text: Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
paragraphs.translation: 很巧妙，不是吗？但也要注意到另一个有趣的讽刺，即验证码被描述为“自动化图灵测试”。你可能记得，图灵测试被构想为一种方式，使人类能够确定机器是否能以一种无法分辨是人还是机器人的方式回应。因此，我们进入了一个机器让我们做戏法来证明自己是人类的世界！

paragraphs.text: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
paragraphs.translation: 这一前所未有的转变最奇怪的方面是它被讨论得多么少。煮蛙的隐喻浮现在脑海中。我们是否被数字技术微妙地条件化，以至于看不到发生在我们身上的事情？我们是否被条件化接受一个由“智能”技术统治的世界，以至于为了便利而交易，最终我们变得有点像机器？

paragraphs.text: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is "yes".
paragraphs.translation: 在最近一本令人震惊且深思熟虑的书中，两位学者——法学教授布雷特·弗里希曼和哲学家埃文·塞林格——认为这个问题的答案是“是”。

paragraphs.text: And they're right. There's nothing technophobic about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.
paragraphs.translation: 他们是对的。这绝非技术恐惧症。我们塑造工具，然后工具塑造我们。技术本应提供服务于人类目的的工具。但是，正如机器学习验证码所展示的，数字技术的很大一部分现在将人类视为实现非我们目的的手段。在这个过程中，他们把我们降低到快乐老鼠在跑步机上奔跑的状态，这些跑步机由不关心我们利益的人设计。所以回到青蛙的隐喻。我们是否足够聪明，在为时已晚之前跳出来？你甚至不需要谷歌来知道答案。

questions.questionText: How did the author respond to the Captcha test?

options.label: A
options.text: He clicked on the cells randomly.

options.label: B
options.text: He accepted the challenge readily.

options.label: C
options.text: He completed it confidently.

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 第二段描述作者面对验证码时虽然有些恼怒（a bit irritated），但还是像绵羊一样照做了（Like a lamb, I complied）。"Like a lamb"比喻顺从地服从，D选项"顺从地完成"最为准确。A选项说随机点击，与原文矛盾；B选项说欣然接受挑战，忽略了作者的不情愿；C选项说自信地完成，原文未体现自信。
questions.keySentence: Like a lamb, I complied.

wrongOptions.A: 作者是按要求正确识别交通标志，并非随机点击。
wrongOptions.B: 作者是a bit irritated（有些恼怒），并非欣然接受。
wrongOptions.C: 原文用Like a lamb形容顺从，并未体现自信。

questions.questionText: What is ironic about the Captcha test?

options.label: A
options.text: A machine can respond to the test as well as humans do.

options.label: B
options.text: A machine can outperform humans in object identification.

options.label: C
options.text: A test designed to test machines is now used by machines to test humans.

options.label: D
options.text: A test conceived to tell a human from a robot can now do tricks humans can't.

questions.analysis: 第四段解释了验证码被称为"自动图灵测试"的讽刺之处：图灵测试最初是让人类判断机器能否像人一样回应，而现在验证码却是机器让人类做把戏来证明自己是人。C选项"一个设计来测试机器的测试现在被机器用来测试人类"准确概括了这一讽刺。A选项说机器能像人一样回应测试，偏离主题；B选项说机器识别物体比人强，原文未提及；D选项说测试能做人类做不到的把戏，曲解原文。
questions.keySentence: So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!

wrongOptions.A: 原文强调的是角色反转的讽刺，并非机器能像人一样应答。
wrongOptions.B: 原文未讨论机器在物体识别上优于人类。
wrongOptions.D: 原文的讽刺在于角色互换，而非测试本身能做人类做不到的事。

questions.questionText: Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog?

options.label: A
options.text: To show that humans are unwilling to trade convenience for control by smart tech.

options.label: B
options.text: To show that humans are unaware of the potential danger brought by smart tech.

options.label: C
options.text: To question whether humans are conditioned to accept digital tech.

options.label: D
options.text: To question whether humans are as vulnerable as the boiling frog.

questions.analysis: 第五段用"温水煮蛙"的比喻来说明人类可能已被数字技术悄然影响而不自知。作者提问"我们是否已被微妙地驯化以至于看不到发生在自己身上的事？"B选项"表明人类没有意识到智能技术带来的潜在危险"最为准确。A选项说人类不愿用便利换取被控制，与原文意思相反（人们恰恰在不知不觉中这样做了）；C选项只是部分表述；D选项把人类与青蛙做简单类比，缺乏对比喻深层含义的理解。
questions.keySentence: Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?

wrongOptions.A: 原文暗示人们在不知不觉中已经用便利换取了被控制，并非不愿意这样做。
wrongOptions.C: 这只是比喻中的一个问题，不是使用该比喻的根本目的。
wrongOptions.D: 比喻的重点是人类对危险的无知觉，而非简单地说人类像青蛙一样脆弱。

questions.questionText: Why does the author think that Brett Frischmann and Evan Selinger are right?

options.label: A
options.text: A large part of digital tech is now making use of humans to meet its own ends.

options.label: B
options.text: Humans are now fast locked in a race against digital tech to control the world.

options.label: C
options.text: Digital tech can serve human needs in ways previously thought impossible.

options.label: D
options.text: Digital tech is now doing thinking while humans are doing repetitive work.

questions.analysis: 第七段作者解释说相当大比例的数字技术现在把人类当作实现其目的的手段，而这些目的并非我们的目的，把我们变成了在跑步轮上跑的快乐老鼠。A选项"大部分数字技术正在利用人类来满足自己的目的"准确对应原文。B选项说人类与数字技术竞争控制世界，原文未提及；C选项说数字技术以不可思议的方式服务人类需求，与原文观点相反；D选项说数字技术在思考而人类做重复劳动，过度简化了原文。
questions.keySentence: A significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours.

wrongOptions.B: 原文未提及人类与数字技术在竞争控制世界。
wrongOptions.C: 原文观点恰恰相反，认为技术在利用人类而非服务人类。
wrongOptions.D: 原文说技术把人当工具使用，并非简单地说技术在思考而人在做重复劳动。

questions.questionText: What does the author imply by asking "Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?" at the end of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: It is not sensible to expect digital tech to take humans' interest to heart.

options.label: B
options.text: It is hard to say whether technology or humans will get the upper hand.

options.label: C
options.text: We may have to search the web to get the answer to the question.

options.label: D
options.text: We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us.

questions.analysis: 文章末尾作者问"我们是否足够聪明能在为时已晚之前跳出来？"紧接着说"你甚至不用谷歌搜索就知道答案"，暗示答案是否定的。结合"温水煮蛙"的比喻，作者暗示我们可能无法及时醒悟数字技术对我们构成的危险。D选项"我们可能无法及时警醒数字技术对我们的危害"最为准确。
questions.keySentence: Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.

wrongOptions.A: 虽然文章提到技术不以人类利益为核心，但这不是末尾问题的暗示重点。
wrongOptions.B: 原文不是在讨论技术和人类谁占上风，而是在暗示人类可能已来不及醒悟。
wrongOptions.C: 作者说不用谷歌就知道答案，意在暗示答案显而易见（是否定的），并非建议去搜索。

questionGroups.sourceText: 节俭是中华民族的传统美德。在中国古代，生产力低下，先人们深知劳动成果来之不易，因而秉持节俭的理念。到了物质极大丰富的今天，中国人民依然坚持节俭的生活方式，体现了理性消费的生活理念和对劳动的尊重。近年来，中国政府持续加强节约型社会的建设，倡导「光盘行动」，减少食物浪费，提倡简约低碳的生活方式，推进资源循环利用，反对过度消费。节约型社会的建设有力地推动了中国经济的高质量发展。

answer.model_translation: Frugality is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. In ancient China, when productivity was low, our ancestors were well aware that the fruits of labor did not come easily, and therefore upheld the concept of frugality. Today, in an era of great material abundance, the Chinese people still adhere to a frugal lifestyle, reflecting the philosophy of rational consumption and respect for labor. In recent years, the Chinese government has continued to strengthen the building of a conservation-oriented society, advocating the "Clean Plate Campaign" to reduce food waste, promoting a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing the recycling of resources, and opposing excessive consumption. The construction of a conservation-oriented society has powerfully driven the high-quality development of China's economy.
answer.translation_analysis: 本段为典型的文化主题说明文，翻译时应注意以下策略：1）准确传达中国特色概念，如「光盘行动」译为 Clean Plate Campaign（已成为通用英文表达）；2）长句拆分与合并——原文多处使用排比和并列结构，英文中可通过分词短语（advocating...promoting...advancing...opposing）保持节奏感；3）抽象概念具体化，如「节约型社会」译为 conservation-oriented society；4）注意时态转换，古代用过去时，现今用现在时，体现时间线的变化。

sentence_breakdown.chinese: 节俭是中华民族的传统美德。
sentence_breakdown.english: Frugality is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation.
sentence_breakdown.note: 简单主系表结构，直译即可。

sentence_breakdown.chinese: 在中国古代，生产力低下，先人们深知劳动成果来之不易，因而秉持节俭的理念。
sentence_breakdown.english: In ancient China, when productivity was low, our ancestors were well aware that the fruits of labor did not come easily, and therefore upheld the concept of frugality.
sentence_breakdown.note: 用 when 引导时间状语从句交代背景，that 引导宾语从句，and therefore 连接因果关系。

sentence_breakdown.chinese: 到了物质极大丰富的今天，中国人民依然坚持节俭的生活方式，体现了理性消费的生活理念和对劳动的尊重。
sentence_breakdown.english: Today, in an era of great material abundance, the Chinese people still adhere to a frugal lifestyle, reflecting the philosophy of rational consumption and respect for labor.
sentence_breakdown.note: 「到了…的今天」处理为 Today, in an era of...；「体现了」用现在分词 reflecting 作伴随状语。

sentence_breakdown.chinese: 近年来，中国政府持续加强节约型社会的建设，倡导「光盘行动」，减少食物浪费，提倡简约低碳的生活方式，推进资源循环利用，反对过度消费。
sentence_breakdown.english: In recent years, the Chinese government has continued to strengthen the building of a conservation-oriented society, advocating the "Clean Plate Campaign" to reduce food waste, promoting a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing the recycling of resources, and opposing excessive consumption.
sentence_breakdown.note: 排比动词统一用现在分词形式（advocating, promoting, advancing, opposing）保持并列结构一致；用现在完成时 has continued 体现「持续」的含义。

sentence_breakdown.chinese: 节约型社会的建设有力地推动了中国经济的高质量发展。
sentence_breakdown.english: The construction of a conservation-oriented society has powerfully driven the high-quality development of China's economy.
sentence_breakdown.note: 「有力地」译为副词 powerfully；用现在完成时表示持续至今的影响。
